cohort: Postpartum patients aged 18-50 years who delivered at George Washington University and underwent a scheduled or emergent cesarean from December 2022 to September 2023.
finding: After excluding one outlier, an increase of 1 mL in quantitative blood loss during cesarean delivery corresponded to an average decrease of 1.83% in average steps per day postpartum.
mod_finding: The study specifically focused on physical activity during cesarean recovery, finding that higher quantitative blood loss during cesarean delivery was associated with decreased postpartum physical activity.
